quotes.quote: To answer these questions, we built an agent-based model that simulates the judgment of decision-makers receiving guidance from a (more or less) biased algorithm or a (more or less) biased and noisy human advisor.
We did 50 simulation runs of each of the 27 parameter combinations to obtain enough variation in the simulated population-level behavior of decision-makers.

G1.rationale: The principal results are produced by running an agent-based simulation model, which a third party can re-run given the model code and parameters.

quotes.quote: The simplest behavioral outcome is the median number of subjects who faced intervention from decision-makers (put in retention) after 6,000 time steps.

G2.rationale: The paper explicitly names the median number of subjects put in retention as the simplest behavioral outcome, and Fig 3 reports these counts across parameter combinations.

quotes.quote: All simulation outputs, scripts used to reproduce the figures, and the full agent-based model code for this study are publicly available from the Open Science Framework (OSF) repository ( https://osf.io/vzmd2 ).

G3.rationale: The deposit listing contains only a README file; it is unclear whether the raw simulation outputs needed to reproduce the target are included among the listed files.

quotes.quote: We use the NetLogo agent-based modeling software [ 69 , 70 ]. Model files and parameter settings will be made available to facilitate replication.
We varied advice bias β A across the ABM simulations between 0 and 2 in intervals of 0.25 – with 0 reflecting an extreme interventionist bias and 2 reflecting a severe non-interventionist bias.

G4.rationale: The Methods section describes the model equations, parameters, and simulation procedure in sufficient detail to implement the model without the original code.

quotes.quote: We use the NetLogo agent-based modeling software [ 69 , 70 ].

G5.rationale: NetLogo is free, open-source software, so no proprietary software is required.

specification.exact_target: Median number of subjects put in retention (true positives + false positives) after 6,000 time steps, reported in Fig 3 for each combination of advice bias β_A (0 to 2 in 0.25 intervals) and advice noise c (0, 0.25, 0.5).
specification.blind_target: The median count of subjects who faced intervention (put in retention) by decision-makers after 6,000 time steps, as a function of advice bias and advice noise, in an agent-based model of human-algorithm decision-making.
specification.target_location: Fig 3 (and Fig 4, Fig 5 for other prior distributions)

location_quotes.quote: the median (line) and the interquartile range (IQR) of 50 simulation runs, holding constant the parameter combinations ( β A , c ).

method_quotes.quote: We use the NetLogo agent-based modeling software [ 69 , 70 ]. Model files and parameter settings will be made available to facilitate replication.
We varied advice bias β A across the ABM simulations between 0 and 2 in intervals of 0.25 – with 0 reflecting an extreme interventionist bias and 2 reflecting a severe non-interventionist bias.
We repeated each run 50 times to obtain enough variation in outcomes to inform us about heterogeneity in decision-makers’ aggregate behavior under similar conditions.

specification.comparison_metric: Compare the median number of subjects put in retention (true positives + false positives) from re-running the agent-based model with the reported medians in Fig 3 for each parameter combination.
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: Counts must match exactly (medians as reported in Fig 3).
specification.specification_gaps: The exact random seed, NetLogo version, and any additional parameter settings (e.g., spatial environment size, subject retention duration) are not fully specified in the text; the paper refers to S1 File for additional details.

alternatives_considered.reason: The paper states the simplest outcome is the median number of subjects put in retention, which includes both true and false positives; true positives alone is a component, not the principal target.
Similarly, false positives is a component of the retention count and not the primary outcome named by the authors.
The IQR is a measure of variability, not the principal quantitative result; the paper focuses on median counts as the main behavioral outcome.
